subject: science
passage: The electric eel of South America is not a true eel but a kind of knifefish. The thousands of specialized cells stacked along the length of its ______ a small voltage each, like batteries connected in a row, and together they can deliver a shock of several hundred volts to stun prey or drive off a predator.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The subject of the second sentence is "The thousands of specialized cells stacked along the length of its body," and its verb is "produce." No punctuation should separate a subject from its verb, even when the subject is long, so nothing goes between "body" and "produce."
explanation.A: Incorrect. A colon must follow a complete sentence; "The thousands of specialized cells stacked along the length of its body" is not one.
explanation.B: Correct. The long subject "The thousands of specialized cells … its body" flows straight into its verb "produce" with no punctuation.
explanation.C: Incorrect. A single comma can't separate a subject from its verb.
explanation.D: Incorrect. A semicolon joins two independent clauses; here it would cut the subject off from its verb.
